resources.string: Lets the coding agent on your PC read the screen and tap for you, always shown on screen with a Pause button. It never reads passwords and never acts in protected apps such as your bank.
Tells you when the agent asks your permission, so you can answer in time.
The ongoing notification with the conversation and its buttons.
Tells you when the agent has finished.
Questions about risky commands, with Allow and Deny.
Looking for your PC… On the PC, run adbuddy serve with wireless debugging on.
Paused: the agent cannot use the phone
This app is too old for the ADBuddy on your PC: install a newer build with adbuddy setup --apk <file> on the PC (plain setup does not replace an installed app)
The ADBuddy on your PC is too old for this app: update it on the PC
Access cut: the PC cannot touch your phone
Not paired with your PC yet. On the PC: adbuddy setup
The PC cannot touch your phone
You cut its access. Give it back when you want the agent to work again.
ADBuddy\'s notifications are off or silenced: you will not be told when the agent asks you something. Turn them on in the system settings.
Allow this same command during the session

Expired: it can no longer be answered.

Open ADBuddy to read the warning and allow it.

resources.string: The PC \"%1$s\" asks to finish setting up ADBuddy. If you accept, it will:
Give ADBuddy the permission to change secure settings, used to cut and restore the PC\'s adb access from the phone.
Exempt ADBuddy from battery optimisation, so the channel with the PC stays open.

Turn on ADBuddy\'s accessibility service: it lets the agent read the screen, tap and type on it, showing a frame and a Pause button while it acts, and never in ADBuddy or in protected apps. Any other service you use stays on.
ADBuddy itself sends nothing outside: the PC and the phone talk through the adb connection you paired. What the coding agent reads goes wherever that agent sends it.
Done. You can go back to the PC.
Done. Two quick steps remain here; then go back to the PC.
Nothing was set up. To try again, run adbuddy setup on the PC.
Nothing yet. Every adb command of the agent will appear here.
Write to the agent below. Risky commands ask for your confirmation.
Debugging is off: the PC cannot reach the phone.
Debugging is back on. If remote mode was on, its network port stays open until the PC connects or the phone restarts.
Debugging could not be turned off. Turn off USB debugging and wireless debugging in Developer options.
Debugging could not be turned back on. Turn it on in Developer options.
Undo it on the PC: adbuddy undo %1$s
No connection with the PC: keys are not sent
There is more text: scroll to its end to answer
Not connected: answer from the PC
Time is up: answer from the PC
The agent starts again with no memory of this one. This conversation stays on the PC.
The file could not be added
Closing… the PC is trying to close port 5555
Unknown: the host will tell when it reconnects
Port 5555 stays open on any network, including public ones, for up to 12 hours. Your PC\'s key is still required. Turn it off when you are back home.
Away from home, turning it off cuts access until you are back on your Wi-Fi.
ADBuddy can tell you when the agent asks your permission or finishes. Without notifications you would only see its questions with the app open, and they expire.
Choose the apps the agent must never read or touch: banking, payments, passwords, 2FA and the apps that receive your codes. ADBuddy itself is always protected.
This list is a proposal made by name. Review it and confirm it: once you do, ADBuddy never changes it by itself.
Looks like banking, payments or passwords
Saved. Until the PC connects it keeps the previous list: apps you just protected are not protected on the PC yet.
Could not read your apps. Nothing was changed; try again.

Lets the agent read what your notifications say, for example to see a message you just received. From protected apps and from ADBuddy it only sees that a notification exists, never what it says. It cannot dismiss or tap any notification. It is optional.
Android allows it; your confirmation is missing
Messages, mail and chat apps that receive your login codes (Gmail, Outlook, Telegram, WhatsApp…) are protected by default, if installed, unless you removed them from the protected apps list.
The agent can read your notifications. You can stop it here, or in the system settings.
The system lets ADBuddy read your notifications, but the agent cannot yet. Confirm here that you want it to. Only you can: the agent cannot press this button.
The agent cannot read your notifications.
ADBuddy cannot tell whether access is allowed, or it is allowed but not active. Open the system settings and turn it off and on again.
Let the agent read my notifications
If the switch is greyed out, open ADBuddy\'s App info, tap the three dots and choose \"Allow restricted settings\".
You can turn it on later in ADBuddy\'s Settings, under Notification access.
Proposed list (%1$d). Review it and confirm.
Choose the language of ADBuddy for this app only
The PC does not support this yet

The agent is busy: try again in a moment
